sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: A very small species, close to E. petilus; compared with the small form of that species: the body is larger, the head more contracted, the rostrum slightly stouter, the head and rostrum uniformly orange red, and the antennae much darker and with much longer segments. The soldier has 12-segmented antennae, occasionally 13, and the mandibles with or without a pointed tooth. The worker is very similar to that of E. petilus, with 15-segmented antennae. The alate is not recorded in the original.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text:
A very small species, close to E. petilus; compared with the small form of that species: the body is larger, the head more contracted, the rostrum slightly stouter, the head and rostrum uniformly orange red, and the antennae much darker and with much longer segments. Antennae 12-segmented, occasionally 13; with 12 segments, segment 2 the shortest of all, only slightly shorter than segment 3; segments 4—11 longer than segment 3, slender, segment 4 sometimes showing a faint trace of subdivision (with 13 segments this subdivision is clear and segment 4 becomes the shortest and narrowest of all). Mandibles with or without a pointed tooth.
Measurements: body length 2.80—3.00 mm; head length (to apex of rostrum) 1.30—1.35 mm; head width 0.55—0.59 mm; pronotum width 0.35—0.40 mm.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text:
Very similar to the worker of E. petilus. Antennae 15-segmented; segment 3 very small. Postclypeus more than half as long as wide.
Measurements: body length 3.50—4.00 mm; head length (to apex of labrum) 1.43—1.60 mm; head length (to clypeofrontal suture) 0.75—0.88 mm; head width 1.17—1.28 mm; pronotum width 0.58—0.70 mm.

note: Rewritten from the English species-level description in Hill (1942); the original gives it as Eutermes kershawi sp. nov., with the text reading "named in honour of Mr. James A. Kershaw" and the type locality Forrest (WA), also recorded from New South Wales: Broken Hill. The heading line was OCRed as 'Eutermes hersliawi' and the figure captions as 'Kerehawi'/'kershawi'; the species is identified from the naming statement and the locality. The alate is recorded as 'Not known' in the original, so that section is not included. OCR misreadings: '4.Q0'='4.00', '1-60'='1.60', '13-segme.nted'='13-segmented', 'pro-notum' broken across lines.
